content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a guideline for the non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults, specifically for use in primary and community care settings. This guideline is available in both electronic and print formats, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-008178-9 and 978-92-4-008179-6. The guideline was coordinated by the Ageing and Health Unit within the Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Ageing (MCA) at WHO headquarters, under the leadership of Anshu Banerjee. Andrew Briggs and Yuka Sumi led the preparation of the document as part of the secretariat. WHO extends its gratitude to the 25 members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG), who contributed their expertise from various institutions and countries. Additionally, WHO acknowledges the contributions of the 14 members of the External Review Group, as well as the systematic review authors and their teams, who provided critical evidence to inform the guideline. The guideline development process was supported by the WHO Steering Group, which included representatives from various WHO departments and regional offices. WHO also thanks the observers from partner organizations who participated in the second GDG meeting in September 2022. This guideline provides evidence-based recommendations for the non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults, with a focus on primary and community care settings. It includes detailed sections on implementation considerations, research implications, dissemination strategies, and monitoring and evaluation of the recommendations' impact.
